text_1_facilitator.eng:
Today’s topic is about teen safety.

Teens can spend a lot of time outside the house or online, where it is harder for us to keep them safe. Talking together about safe and unsafe places — and how to prevent problems — really helps.

media_title.eng: Why is teen safety important for you and your family?

media_transcript.eng:
Greetings, everyone.

Today our topic is teen safety 

It is our responsibility as parents to try to keep our teens safe and help them to keep themselves safe. An important part of that is that we are all aware of the safe and unsafe areas in our communities.

It is also our responsibility to ensure that they understand the dangers that they might be exposed to when they are online. That way our teenagers will be responsible and be able to make right decisions to keep themselves safe too.

rows.media_title: Why is teen safety important for you and your family?
rows.media_transcript:
Greetings, everyone.

Today our topic is teen safety 

It is our responsibility as parents to try to keep our teens safe and help them to keep themselves safe. An important part of that is that we are all aware of the safe and unsafe areas in our communities.

It is also our responsibility to ensure that they understand the dangers that they might be exposed to when they are online. That way our teenagers will be responsible and be able to make right decisions to keep themselves safe too.

text_1_facilitator.eng:
Sometimes our teens notice things about their surroundings that we don’t. By talking and listening, we can better understand their world and guide them through challenges – including the risks they face online.

With our support, they can learn to stay safe and make good decisions. 

This guidance is important for both girls and boys. Abuse can happen in different ways — including sexual abuse.

text_2.eng: _Child sexual abuse can happen in different ways. It can happen when someone touches a child in a sexual way, makes sexual comments or requests, pressures or forces a child, or offers money or gifts to ask for sexual things. It can happen face-to-face or online._

media_title.eng: A safety plan helped @data.characters.media_female_8.name protect her teen. Tap play to hear more

media_transcript.eng:
I was so grateful to make the safety plan with my teen. I thought I knew which areas are safe for my teen and which are not. But when we made the safety plan together, I realised that my girl knew more areas that I was not aware of.

I also thought she was safe at school, but through this activity I realised she was being bullied and the teachers did not do anything about it.

The more we talked, the more I understood and got information from my teen. That really helped me to protect my teen and keep her safe.

rows.media_transcript:
I was so grateful to make the safety plan with my teen. I thought I knew which areas are safe for my teen and which are not. But when we made the safety plan together, I realised that my girl knew more areas that I was not aware of.

I also thought she was safe at school, but through this activity I realised she was being bullied and the teachers did not do anything about it.

The more we talked, the more I understood and got information from my teen. That really helped me to protect my teen and keep her safe.
rows.text_2: _Child sexual abuse can happen in different ways. It can happen when someone touches a child in a sexual way, makes sexual comments or requests, pressures or forces a child, or offers money or gifts to ask for sexual things. It can happen face-to-face or online._

text_1_facilitator.eng:
The most important way to help keep your teen safe is to make sure that they know they can talk to you about anything. 

Work with your teen to notice risks — like when someone pressures or makes them feel uncomfortable, online or offline.

**Let’s look at examples of risky situations to help you spot warning signs.**

To keep our teens safe, we need to understand the dangerous situations they could get into! 

Let’s get practical now, and draw a map of safe and unsafe places. You can include: 
- 🗺️ Places from your community
- 🌐 Apps/websites you use online

text_1_facilitator.eng: Step 1: Draw all the important places in your community.

text_2.eng:
Draw a map of your teen’s community, with pictures of all the main places like streets, your house, school, shops, places your teen visits.

Remember to include your phone and other internet devices, as mobile apps and websites are also places where you and your teen can spend a lot of time!

Remember to include your phone and other internet devices, as mobile apps and websites are also places where you and your teen can spend a lot of time!

text_1_facilitator.eng: Step 2: Choose which places are safe and unsafe.

text_2.eng:
- Which areas on your map are safe for teenagers? CIRCLE these
- Which areas on your map are unsafe for teenagers? CROSS those off
- What makes a place safe or unsafe? Is this different for boys and girls? 
- Looking at the places you mapped out, what rules could you come up with together to help your teen stay safe?

text_1_facilitator.eng:
Now that we understand our safe and unsafe places better, let's look at an example where something simple, like a Safety Word, can help keep your teen safe. 

First, think back to when you were a teenager. Was there ever a time when you were in danger but you could not tell your family because they would have been angry?

This ALMOST happened to @data.characters.f1_son_18.name and @data.characters.f1_daughter_16.name! Let’s have a look:

character_1_text.eng: Don’t tell the adults, but I am going to a bar with my friends tonight.

character_2_text.eng: Have fun! I told them I am staying with my girlfriend, but I am actually going to a cool party.

Now that we understand our safe and unsafe places better, let's look at an example where something simple, like a Safety Word, can help keep your teen safe. 

First, think back to when you were a teenager. Was there ever a time when you were in danger but you could not tell your family because they would have been angry?

This ALMOST happened to @data.characters.f1_son_18.name and @data.characters.f1_daughter_16.name! Let’s have a look:
rows.character_1_text: Don’t tell the adults, but I am going to a bar with my friends tonight.
rows.character_2_text: Have fun! I told them I am staying with my girlfriend, but I am actually going to a cool party.

character_1_text.eng: I think they are dealing drugs. We could all get arrested. But I can’t tell my parents – they will be so angry!

rows.character_1_text: I think they are dealing drugs. We could all get arrested. But I can’t tell my parents – they will be so angry!

character_1_text.eng: I am scared. Everyone is too drunk to drive me home. This guy says he will take me, but he wants us to go to his house first. I can’t tell my parents – I lied about coming to this party.

rows.character_1_text: I am scared. Everyone is too drunk to drive me home. This guy says he will take me, but he wants us to go to his house first. I can’t tell my parents – I lied about coming to this party.

text_1_facilitator.eng: These are dangerous situations! Thankfully, @data.characters.f1_son_18.name and @data.characters.f1_daughter_16.name then remembered what their father told them:

character_1_text.eng:
I care about your safety more than anything. If you are ever upset, or scared, you can always call me for help, or tell me about it.

Shall we use an imaginary ‘Aunty Cecilia’ as our Safety Word? Just say something about Aunty Cecilia, I promise that I will try my best to help and I will not be angry – even if you are doing something you shouldn't be doing.

text_1_facilitator.eng: Here are some skills to help you keep your teen safe!

section_1_text.eng: Make a map with your teen of safe and unsafe areas in your community and online. You and your teen may have different ideas and experiences – try to be open and learn from each other

section_2_text.eng: Make rules with your teen about how they can stay safe in your community (especially in risky areas that cannot be avoided), and how they can safely use the apps and websites that they like.

section_2_extra_text.eng: Explore with your teen if you can create a rule around sharing with a trusted adult when something feels wrong. This can really help them stay safe in person and online.

section_3_text.eng: Agree on a Safety Word. If something happens that makes your teen upset, uncomfortable or scared, they can say the Safety Word and you will help them without getting angry or punishing them, even if they were doing something wrong.

section_3_extra_text.eng:
What Safety Word can you choose with your teen? Here are some ideas from other families:

🥑 A specific food
👵🏽 A specific family member
🐒 A specific animal
🤔 Something else

text_1_facilitator.eng:
If you have not done it together yet, this week's home assignment is to make a map with your teen of safe and unsafe places. You can include places from your community 🗺️ and even apps and websites your teen uses online 🌐.

Make sure you are both happy with the safety plan. What really matters is that you talk with your teen as you do this – often teens know much more than we do about where it is safe and unsafe!

quiz_1_question.eng: Can you make a safety map with your teen and talk about ways to stay safe online and in your community?

quiz_1_feedback_1.eng: That's great! Taking the time to map out safe and unsafe places together helps your teen feel more confident and supported.

quiz_1_feedback_2.eng: You can do it! Even starting the conversation is a big step towards helping your teen stay safe.

quiz_1_feedback_3.eng: That's okay. It can feel hard at first, but small talks about safety make a big difference. Try again when you feel ready.

text_1_facilitator.eng: When teens know they can turn to us without fear, they are more likely to ask for help when something feels unsafe - both offline and online. Talking calmly and making safety plans together builds trust that lasts.

media_title.eng: Safety planning helped @data.characters.media_daughter_7.name open up. Hear her story

media_transcript.eng:
When my friends or I got into trouble, I would always try to hide it from my mother because she would get so angry and shout at me.

When we made the map of safe and unsafe places, I learnt a lot – also why it is dangerous to share every picture online. My mother told me I can always ask her if there is a problem and she promised she would not get mad.

She kept her promise, so now if I have a problem or I do not feel safe I know we can always come up with a solution together. I can even talk to my mother about the things I do online now!
